content:
Rumors suggest that Apple's iPhone lineup this fall will be headlined by the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Below are the three most important feature differences, aside from price, that could influence your decision on whether to upgrade.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This is the most obvious distinction, but it's still worth highlighting because it's also the most crucial difference.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic design that iPhones have used for years. Reports indicate that their screen sizes and overall appearance will be identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. Its body design is entirely different—the outer screen is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner screen resembles an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Line Continues to Lead

Apple has consistently equipped its Pro lineup with the most advanced and innovative camera technology. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to have camera specs largely similar to those of the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not feature a telephoto lens.

Sources indicate that the iPhone Ultra will still sport the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro series, and rumors suggest its performance will be even better this year.

Performance: Both Feature the A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Affect Real-World Performance

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to be powered by the same A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, their performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will retain the all-aluminum unibody design introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, along with a vapor chamber for cooling. These two changes led to a notable improvement in overall performance for the iPhone 17 Pro compared to its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures during heavy workloads.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a lightweight titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, though only one leaker has mentioned this so far. Due to the different materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may deliver slightly lower performance under direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
